coverage.evidence: Every bot.* form takes no argument. BotRow.RenderAsync returns null when arguments.Count > 0 (server/src/NomNomzBot.Infrastructure/Platform/Templating/Helpers/Bot/BotRow.cs:73-74). A null result prints the token as written (Rendering/TemplateTreeRenderer.cs:117-118). So {bot.name:x} stays literal. The keys come from the provider rows (BotTemplateHelpers.cs:43-48, namespace 'bot' at :51): BotIdentityHelpers.cs:19-24, BotCommandHelpers.cs:22-54, BotUptimeHelpers.cs:19-42, BotChannelHelpers.cs:20-37. Legacy {botname} is in TemplateHelperRegistry.cs:614.

Fixed texts: BotText.cs:25 and :27. Version: the informational version cut at '+' (RuntimeBotProcessInfo.cs:33-44). An unknown value prints empty (BotText.cs:21). Personality: the value is capitalized (BotChannelHelpers.cs:24; StreamText.cs:149-150), from the five tones (Domain/Identity/Enums/PersonalityTone.cs:28-46). Language falls back to 'en' (BotChannelHelpers.cs:29). Dashboard: link is {origin}/app/u/{channel} (BotText.cs:58-59). It is empty with no public origin (BotChannelHelpers.cs:46-48; BotText.cs:44-55). Timers: enabled count (BotData.cs:148). Both counts use N0 in the channel culture (People/PeopleText.cs:24; BotChannelHelpers.cs:58; BotCommandHelpers.cs:71; BotRow.cs:26).

Every bot row registers TemplateHelperContexts.Standard (BotRow.cs:77). Standard is every context except Viewer (Application/Abstractions/Templating/TemplateHelperContexts.cs:21-22). That means Command, EventResponse, Timer, Pipeline, Discord and Webhook (TemplateHelperContext.cs:21-63). {botname} uses AllContexts, the same six without Viewer (TemplateHelperRegistry.cs:32-40, :614). The feature label 'Viewer Templates' is at FeatureService.cs:92-93.

{bot.name} and {bot.mention} read the enabled twitch_bot service row, with fallback 'NomNomzBot' (DbBotIdentityDirectory.cs:22-41; BotIdentityHelpers.cs:19-20, 27-28). This read is not per channel and is not the speaking-bot resolver. {botname} reads the same row (Legacy/LegacyTemplateHelpers.cs:1405-1422). The speaking bot is the channel's custom bot, else the shared bot (Identity/ChannelTwitchBotResolver.cs:31-53). With neither, NoDedicatedBot applies and the streamer's own account speaks (IBotModeratorStatusReader.cs:19-20). isMod is true for Moderator or NoDedicatedBot, false for NotModerator, else empty (BotIdentityHelpers.cs:34-42). A status recorded for a replaced bot reads as NotObserved (BotModeratorStatusReader.cs:47-52). Checks run at sync on join and every 5 minutes (BackgroundServices/BotLifecycleService.cs:208-216, 456-462), plus on Twitch role events (Identity/EventHandlers/BotModeratorRoleChangeHandler.cs). The sidebar entry White-label bot is in the Bot group (dashboard/src/layouts/dashboard/settingsNavigation.ts:55-61; i18n en.json:898). The card title is "Your channel's own bot" (views/dashboard/settings/white-label-bot/i18n/en.json:5).

Only enabled custom commands are cached (Platform/ChannelRegistry.cs:449-452). Regex commands are left out. An alias collapses through Distinct. Commands sort by name, case-insensitive, and carry their channel, custom or no prefix (BotCommands.cs:29-39, 74-80; ChannelRegistry.cs:563-565). Built-ins: only enabled ones, always with the channel prefix, in catalog order, not sorted (BotCommands.cs:42-55; Commands/BuiltinCommandService.cs:65; BuiltinCommandCatalog.cs:32). The full list puts custom commands first and shows each trigger once (BotCommands.cs:58-61). forUser filters by the user.role seed, and level <= role (BotCommands.cs:64-68; BotCommandHelpers.cs:40-53). An empty role means Everyone (Domain/Identity/ChatRole.cs:77). user.role is seeded only on chat paths (Chat/EventHandlers/ChatMessageHandler.cs:537, 1050, 1631; Commands/CommandInvoker.cs:504). When the built-in read fails, the lists and the count are empty (BotData.cs:132; BotCommandHelpers.cs:61-80). The custom list does not need the built-ins (BotCommandHelpers.cs:28-33).

Uptime counts from process start (RuntimeBotProcessInfo.cs:22-30; BotUptimeHelpers.cs:45-46). Short format: 'Xd Yh' from a day up, else 'Hh Mm', 'Mm Ss' or 'Ss' (BotText.cs:34-35; Stream/StreamText.cs:68-75). Long format: Humanize with 2 units in the channel culture (StreamText.cs:23, 36-37). startedAt uses yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm in the channel zone, else UTC (BotText.cs:38-41; StreamText.cs:106-109). lastRestart.relative rounds to the nearest day, hour or minute (StreamText.cs:91-103). channel.loadedAgo uses the same span style from ChannelContext.LoadedAt (BotUptimeHelpers.cs:35-42; ChannelRegistry.cs:100). A channel is evicted when it is offline and idle for 2 hours (ChannelRegistry.cs:42-44, 725-730).

reader_answers.evidence: forUser filters by the invoker's role (BotCommandHelpers.cs:40-53; BotCommands.cs:64-68). The identity helpers are those in BotIdentityHelpers.cs:19-24. No form takes an argument (BotRow.cs:73-74).

The contexts are Standard, every context but Viewer (BotRow.cs:77; TemplateHelperContexts.cs:21-22; TemplateHelperContext.cs:21-63). The no-argument rule is BotRow.cs:73-74 with TemplateTreeRenderer.cs:117-118.

{bot.name} reads the install's twitch_bot service row, not the channel or the speaking-bot resolver. It falls back to NomNomzBot (DbBotIdentityDirectory.cs:22-41). forUser filters by role (BotCommands.cs:64-68).

The help example uses forUser, which checks only the minimum level, not cooldowns (BotCommands.cs:64-68). Timers and event responses seed no user.role, so the role parses to Everyone (ChatRole.cs:77; the only user.role seeds are in ChatMessageHandler.cs and CommandInvoker.cs:504). {bot.name} is not the posting account (DbBotIdentityDirectory.cs:32-36 vs ChannelTwitchBotResolver.cs:31-53).
